correctness.rationale: The operator preserves constants. Positive threshold layers yield an exact cut norm. Fixed-cut Gini is convex in every rate, so a rate-cube maximizer is binary. For a k-versus-m cut with r and s refreshed sites, the exact output difference from km is [k s(m-k-s)+m r(k-m-r)]/n. The smaller-side refresh count is zero at the maximum; integer quadratic optimization and even/odd monotonicity prove that a singleton cut maximizes the rate-cube norm. An explicit binary-rate singleton attains the formula for all n; mixing it with an all-rows uniform reset yields a strictly positive stochastic matrix whose Gini ratio still exceeds one for n>=4. Exact rational checker independently tests 86,360 extreme cut/rate pairs and further rational and symbolic witness cases. The proof, not finite tests, proves all dimensions.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: For three coordinates Gini is exactly twice oscillation, but in four or more it is a genuinely different quotient norm. originality.rationale: Comparison against the identified primary literature, targeted published-record searches and accessible earlier Gini/Markov operator statements found no formula or stronger implication covering the independent heterogeneous common-mean refresh family. Gaubert and Qu handle a different seminorm and its dual, while Boyd et al. handle doubly stochastic pairwise gossip. The all-rate exact factor and full-support amplifying witness are not implied by those statements. Residual risk is unindexed historical equivalence.
residual_risks: A published equivalent under a different term such as mean absolute difference or simultaneous heterogeneous relaxation may be unindexed and has not been ruled out.
Generalisations to arbitrary stochastic kernels or weighted distributions are outside this theorem.

value.rationale: A natural heterogeneous mean-refresh operator family exhibits a sharp four-agent onset and an exact all-dimensional rate-independent cap approaching 5/4. Most importantly even entrywise strictly positive Doeblin kernels in this family can amplify the complete-pair Gini signal norm, separating established robust oscillation contraction from dispersion stability. Explicit optimal polarized updates and an attained fixed-dimension formula make the boundary useful for finite consensus/Markov operator stability analysis.
